en: The Theravāda Vinaya:
The Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga,
Chapter on Saṅghādisesa Offenses.
13. The Second Training Rule on Evil Conduct At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was staying at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, having been formally admonished by the Saṅgha, spoke to the bhikkhunīs thus:
“Venerable ladies, you should live in association; do not live apart.
There are other bhikkhunīs in the Saṅgha who are of such conduct, such reputation, and such fame, who harass the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha and conceal each other’s faults, yet the Saṅgha says nothing to them.
It is only to you that the Saṅgha speaks out of contempt, disdain, impatience, gossiping, and weakness, saying: ‘Sisters…’”
“They live in close association, of evil conduct, of evil reputation, of evil fame;
they are harassers of the community of bhikkhunīs and concealers of each other’s offenses. ‘Separate yourselves, noble ladies! The Saṅgha of sisters praises seclusion alone.
Those bhikkhunīs who were few in desires... [and so on]... complained, grumbled, and became indignant:
“How indeed can the noble lady Thullanandā, having been formally admonished by the Saṅgha, speak thus to the bhikkhunīs:
‘Venerable ladies, you should live in association; do not live apart.
There are other bhikkhunīs in the Saṅgha as well... [and so forth].
“Live secluded, venerable ladies. The Saṅgha praises seclusion for you, sisters.
… [as before] … “Is it true, monks, that the nun Thullanandā, having been formally reprimanded by the Saṅgha, speaks thus to the nuns:
‘Venerable ladies, live in association; do not live apart’?”
There are other bhikkhunīs in the Saṅgha who are of such conduct, such reputation, and such fame, who harass the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha and conceal each other’s faults; yet the Saṅgha says nothing to them.
But to you alone the Saṅgha speaks thus out of contempt, disdain, impatience, carping, and weakness:
“These sisters live in close association, of evil conduct, evil reputation, and evil fame, harassing the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha.”
“Each other’s offenses you conceal. ‘Live apart, noble ladies; the Saṅgha praises seclusion for sisters,’ was it not so?
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them … [as before] …
"How indeed, monks, could the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, having been formally admonished by the Saṅgha, speak thus to the bhikkhunīs:
'Venerable ladies, live in association; do not live apart.
There are other bhikkhunīs in the Saṅgha as well... [as before]...
"Live secluded, venerable ladies; the Saṅgha praises seclusion for you, sisters.
"This, monks, does not lead to the confidence of those without confidence...
And so, monks, the nuns should recite this training rule thus:"
“Whatever nun should speak thus:
‘Venerable ladies, you should live in association; do not live apart.
There are other nuns in the Saṅgha who are of such conduct, such speech, and such behavior, who harass the community of nuns and conceal each other’s offenses, yet the Saṅgha says nothing to them.’”
"It is you yourselves whom the Saṅgha speaks thus out of contempt, disdain, impatience, frivolity, and weakness:
'The sisters live in close association, of evil conduct, of evil reputation, of evil renown;
they are harassers of the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha and concealers of each other's faults. Depart, noble ladies! The Saṅgha praises seclusion for the sisters.'"
That bhikkhunī should be addressed by the bhikkhunīs thus:
“Venerable lady, do not speak thus:
‘Venerable lady, you two should live in association; do not live separately.’”

There are other bhikkhunīs in the Saṅgha who behave in this way, who have such a reputation, who have such a repute, who harass the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha, and who conceal each other’s faults. Yet the Saṅgha says nothing to them.
But to you alone the Saṅgha speaks thus out of contempt, disdain, impatience, carping, and weakness:
“These sisters live in close association, of evil conduct, of evil reputation, of evil repute; they harass the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha.”
‘One another is a concealer of faults. Separate yourselves, venerable ladies! The Saṅgha praises seclusion for sisters.

If that bhikkhunī, being thus addressed by the bhikkhunīs, should persist as before, that bhikkhunī is to be formally admonished by the bhikkhunīs up to three times for the sake of relinquishing that [behavior].
If, being admonished up to three times, she relinquishes it, that is good.

If she does not relinquish it, this nun also has committed an offense that is a *saṅghādisesa*, which involves formal meeting of the Saṅgha and entails banishment, after having been charged up to the third time.
"Whoever" means whichever such person... [and so on].
"A bhikkhunī" ...
[as before] ... this is the kind of bhikkhunī intended in this context.
"Should speak thus": [as before].
“Venerable ladies, you should live in association; do not live apart.

There are other bhikkhunīs in the Saṅgha who are of such conduct, such reputation, and such renown, who harass the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha and conceal each other’s faults, yet the Saṅgha says nothing to them.
But it is to you alone that the Saṅgha has contempt.”
"By contempt" means by way of being treated with disdain. "By humiliation" means by way of being subjected to subjugation.
"By impatience" means by anger.
"By frivolity" means...
Made public.
"Weakness" means being without partisans.
He spoke thus:
"Sisters, you are living in association, of evil conduct, of evil reputation, and of evil fame; you are harassers of the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha and concealers of each other's faults.
Separate yourselves, noble ladies! The Saṅgha praises seclusion for the sisters."
"That bhikkhunī" refers to whichever bhikkhunī speaks in such a manner.
"By the bhikkhunīs" refers to...
Other bhikkhunīs [should intervene]. Those who see or hear [her] should say to her:
"Venerable lady, do not speak thus:
'Venerable ladies, you should live in association; do not live separately.'"
“There are other bhikkhunīs in the Saṅgha as well...
… ‘Withdraw, venerable ladies. The Saṅgha praises seclusion for the sisters.
This should be said a second time as well.
A third time she should be told.
If she relinquishes it, that is well;
if she does not relinquish it, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If they do not speak after hearing it, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
That nun, even if she has been dragged into the midst of the Saṅgha, should be told:
"Venerable lady, do not speak thus."
“Venerable ladies, you should live in association; do not live apart.
There are other bhikkhunīs in the Saṅgha as well...
[as before] ... Venerable ladies, separate yourselves. The Saṅgha praises seclusion for the sisters.”
It should be said a second time.
It should be said a third time.
If she relinquishes it, that is good.
If she does not relinquish it, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
That bhikkhunī is to be formally admonished.
"And thus, monks, is she to be formally admonished."
The Saṅgha should be informed by a competent and capable bhikkhunī:
“Let the noble Saṅgha hear me.
This bhikkhunī named so-and-so, having been formally admonished by the Saṅgha, speaks thus to the bhikkhunīs:”
“Venerable ladies, you should live in association; do not live apart.
There are other bhikkhunīs in the Saṅgha who are of such conduct, such reputation, and such renown, who cause trouble for the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha and conceal each other’s offenses.”
The Saṅgha said nothing at all.
It was only out of contempt, disdain, impatience, loquacity, and weakness that the Saṅgha spoke thus to you:
"Sisters, you live in close association, of evil conduct, of evil reputation, of evil fame; you are harassers of the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha and concealers of each other’s faults."
“Live apart, sisters!
The Saṅgha praises seclusion for you.
Yet she did not relinquish that course of action.
If it seems appropriate to the Saṅgha, let the Saṅgha formally admonish the bhikkhunī named so-and-so for the relinquishing of that matter.
This is the motion.
Let the noble Saṅgha hear me.
This bhikkhunī named so-and-so, having been formally admonished by the Saṅgha, speaks thus to the bhikkhunīs:
“Venerable ladies, you should dwell in association;
do not dwell apart.”
There are other bhikkhunīs in the Saṅgha who are of such conduct, such reputation, and such renown, who harass the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha and conceal each other’s faults;
yet the Saṅgha says nothing to them.
But to you alone the Saṅgha speaks thus out of contempt, disdain, impatience, carping, and weakness.
"Sisters, you live in close association, of evil conduct, of evil reputation, and of evil fame; you harass the Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs and conceal each other’s faults.
Separate yourselves, noble ladies!
The Saṅgha praises seclusion for the sisters."
She does not relinquish that matter.
The Saṅgha exhorts the nun so-and-so for the relinquishment of that matter.
Whichever noble lady approves of the exhortation of the nun so-and-so for the relinquishment of that matter, let her be silent.
Whoever does not approve of this, let her speak.
For the second time I speak this matter...
For the third time I speak this matter... [as before].
“The Saṅgha has formally admonished the bhikkhunī so-and-so for the relinquishing of that matter.
It is pleasing to the Saṅgha; therefore, by silence, I hold it thus.
There is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa) for the motion.
With two proclamations there are thullaccaya offenses;
at the conclusion of the proclamation, there is an offense entailing suspension (saṅghādisesa).
For one who commits a saṅghādisesa offense, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa) for the motion; with the two proclamations, the thullaccaya offenses are extinguished.
This too is said with reference to the previous [instances].
"Up to the third time" means:
If one commits [the offense] after being exhorted up to the third time, it is not [an offense] involving conduct that has abandoned the basis.
"Leading to expulsion" means one is expelled from the Saṅgha.
*Saṅghādisesa*:

Only the Saṅgha grants the *mānatta* penance for that offense, sends one back to the beginning, or rehabilitates one; it is not granted by several [monks] nor by a single nun. Therefore it is called "an offense entailing suspension" (*saṅghādisesa*).
It is also a designation and a synonym for that very class of offenses; for that reason too it is called "an offense entailing suspension."
If, regarding a legitimate legal act, one perceives it as a legitimate legal act and does not relinquish [the offense], there is an offense entailing suspension (saṅghādisesa).
If, regarding a legitimate legal act, one is doubtful and does not relinquish it, there is an offense entailing suspension.
If, regarding a legitimate legal act, one perceives it as an illegitimate legal act and does not relinquish it, there is an offense entailing suspension.
If it is an illegal act and one perceives it as a legal act, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If it is an illegal act and one is uncertain of it, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If it is an illegal act and one perceives it as an illegal act, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
There is no offense for one who does not admonish,
or for one who relinquishes [the matter].
"Of one who is insane," "of one who is a first-offender.
The tenth Saṅghādisesa training rule is concluded.
Venerable ladies, the seventeen rules on formal meetings of the Saṅgha (saṅghādisesa) have been recited:
nine that entail immediate offense, and eight that become offenses after the third admonition.
Whichever of these offenses a bhikkhunī commits, that bhikkhunī must undergo the *mānatta* penance for a fortnight before both Saṅghas.
Once she has completed the *mānatta*, that bhikkhunī is to be rehabilitated where there is a community of twenty bhikkhunīs.
If a community of bhikkhunīs is short of even one member of the group of twenty and should rehabilitate that bhikkhunī, [the act is invalid].
That nun is not reproved, and those nuns are to be censured; this is the proper course in such a case.
Therefore, noble ladies, I ask you:
"Are you pure in this matter?"
A second time I ask:
"Are you pure in this matter?
A third time I ask:
“Are you pure in this matter?
“The venerable ones are pure in this matter; therefore they are silent. Thus do I understand it.
The Seventeenfold [Section] is finished.
The section on Saṅghādisesa offenses in the Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga is concluded.
